The diagnosis of cellulitis you were given does not explain the presence of blisters on your forearm combined with mucosal ulcers; those are distinct from the red, warm swelling of a bacterial skin infection. I need to clarify the nature of the skin lesions: do the forearm blisters look like small fluid-filled vesicles on an itchy base, or are they larger, tense, and painful? Also, have you noticed any new skin rashes, such as red rings or target-like spots, elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Tissue_Biopsy: Histopathology shows acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Direct_Fluorescence_Antibody: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris

The biopsy results showing acantholysis and intercellular IgG/C3 deposition are classic for Pemphigus Vulgaris, which explains both the painful mucosal ulcers and the fragile, flaccid blisters on your forearm. Given the severity of this autoimmune condition, please ensure you avoid trauma to the affected areas and seek immediate treatment with systemic corticosteroids.
